Dear {supplier} team,

Our stock of {item:item} is {onhand:n0} {unit:unit}, enough for about {lasts:dur}, and demand is rising. Please tell us the earliest delivery date and how much you can deliver within {lead:n0} days, ideally with fast shipping.

Best regards,
Procurement

Dear {supplier} team,

Our order {po} for {qty:n0} {unit:unit} of {item:item}, placed on {order_date:date}, is now late and expected on {eta:date}. We have only {onhand:n0} {unit:unit} left, enough for about {lasts:dur}, and production would stop in about {hours:dur}.

Please (1) confirm a firm delivery date and (2) send the first available quantity right away.

As a stopgap we could also take {alt:item}. Please tell us if it is available and how fast.

Best regards,
Procurement

Our stock of {item:item} is {onhand:n0} {unit:unit}, below the {ss:n0} we want to keep. Please prioritise our next order and confirm the delivery date.

Best regards,
Procurement

help.title: Help
help.tour_text: A short tour of the screen in 6 steps.
guide.title: Welcome to SmartStock
guide.s1.b: The clock at the top shows the simulated date and hour. Press Start and the warehouse works hour by hour: items are used, deliveries arrive, batches expire.
guide.s2.b: “1 hour = 5 seconds” is the speed. Open Speed to make it faster or slower. You can pause at any time. The clock pauses by itself when something critical happens.
guide.s3.b: “Needs your decision” lists what the system suggests: orders and messages to suppliers. Each card says why, what happens if you approve, and what happens if you do nothing.
guide.s4.b: Every item has a status with an icon: Critical, Running low, OK, Too much, Expiring soon. “Lasts” tells you how long the stock will last at the current use.
guide.s5.b: After you approve or reject, an Undo button appears for a few seconds. “After your decisions” shows what each decision led to. The ? button brings back this tour, the demo and the glossary.
demo.intro: Follow these steps to see the whole story in about two minutes.
demo.s1: Look at the top: it is 5 October, midnight. Under “What is at risk” you see which items may run out.
demo.s2: Press Start. Movements appear under “What happened recently”. Try Speed → 1 s.
demo.s3: When frozen shrimp shells run out, the clock pauses and says why. Read the red message.
demo.s4: In “Needs your decision”, open the order for that item and press the green button to approve it.
demo.s5: Reject another order and keep running: see how the shortage grows because nothing was ordered.
demo.s6: Use More → Jump to next day to see the approved delivery arrive at its hour.
demo.s7: Open “After your decisions” to read, in plain sentences, what each of your choices led to.
demo.s8: Now open the second section, “Space”. The bar at the top shows the steps: Forecast, Decide, Listing, Offers, Leases. The highlighted step is what to do next.
gl.lasts.def: How long the stock on hand lasts if we keep using it at the recent rate.
gl.order_point.def: The stock level at which a new order should be placed so it arrives before we run out.
gl.lead.def: The number of days a supplier needs to deliver after we order.
gl.safety.def: The minimum amount we want to always have on hand, in case demand or delivery surprises us.
gl.overstock.def: More stock than we will use for many weeks. The system does not order more of it.
gl.expiring.def: A batch whose expiry date is close and which we may not use in time.
gl.lot.def: A quantity of an item received together, with one expiry date.
gl.lease.def: Space we rent out to another company for a number of months.
gl.rentable.def: Space nobody is using, which is not kept for our own growth and is allowed to be rented out.
gl.buffer.def: Space we deliberately keep empty for our own future stock.
gl.season.def: How much higher demand is expected in the busy months, for example ×1.8 means 80% more.
gl.spike.def: Use that is more than double what it normally was in the previous weeks.
gl.critical_level.def: How essential an item is for production. A is essential, B important, C can wait.
gl.forecast.def: Our estimate of how much will be used in the coming weeks, based on recent use and the season.

demo.s9: In “Needs your decision” the forecast shows space we will not need. Press “List … for rent”, check the price (an assumed figure) and publish. Nothing from the companies is visible before this.
demo.s10: Press Start and wait one or two simulated days. A company sends an offer. Read the six checks, then accept it, send a counter-offer or reject it.
demo.s11: After you accept, the area is held for the rental dates and the rent is counted every day under “Rentals and income”.
demo.s12: Go back to Purchasing and approve a large order for a general-storage item: if it needs space you listed, a warning appears in both sections. A signed rental always comes first.
guide.s6.b: Purchasing is about stock and orders. Space is about renting out empty warehouse space: forecast, list, offers, rentals. Each has its own decisions, numbers and activity; the clock is shared.

agentdef.forecast.role: Turns the movement history into weekly usage, a seasonal forecast and flags for sudden demand jumps.
agentdef.replenishment.role: Decides which items need an order, how much and in what order, within the free budget and the room of each zone.
agentdef.space-optimization.role: Works out, zone by zone, how much area the stock uses, how much is held back and how much can be rented out.
agentdef.alerts.role: Raises a warning for every risk: what is wrong, why, and what happens if it is ignored. Drafts supplier messages for the serious ones.
agentdef.space-forecast.role: Looks ahead for space the company will not need, keeps what it must keep, and flags conflicts between rentals and purchasing.

agents.flow.title: The flow
agents.flow.text: Five agents run one after the other. They never call each other: each reads the shared database, writes its result there, and the coordinator hands over to the next one. Every agent logs four stages: what it READ, what it decided (REASON), what it wrote (ACT), and the result of its own check (VERIFY). If a check fails the agent runs once more, and if it still fails you see a warning.
agents.flow.human_text: The agents only propose. Nothing is ordered, rented or sent until a person approves it. Every approval is stored with its simulated time and can be followed in “After your decisions”.

gl.agent.def: A small program that reads the database, applies rules, writes its result and checks itself. The five agents hand work to each other through the database; they do not use an AI model.
gl.stages.def: The four stages every agent logs: what it read, what it decided, what it wrote, and the result of its own check.
gl.verify.def: A quick test an agent runs on its own result. If it fails the agent runs again once; if it still fails, a warning is shown and the simulation goes on.
gl.draft.def: A ready-to-send message: the order to a supplier after you approve a purchase, or the reply to a company after you decide on its offer. You can edit it; the app never sends it.
gl.summary.def: One card built from the database after the 08:00 run: top risks, decisions waiting, budget, space and offers.
demo.s13: Open “Agents” under “More”: every run shows its four stages (Read, Reason, Act, Verify) for each of the five agents, with a check mark or a cross for its own check.
demo.s14: Open Help, then “How the agents work”: the flow, one card per agent (what it reads and writes, when it runs, its last self-check) and where you approve.
demo.s15: After you approve an order or answer an offer, open “Drafts”: the message to the supplier or the company is ready in both languages. Edit it, send it yourself, and mark it as sent.
